title: Kenapa Jam Komputer Selalu Reset ke 1 Januari 1970? ⏱️ #artificialintelligence #belajarkoding
description:
Pernah ngalamin laptop atau HP tiba-tiba lempar lu balik ke zaman purba (1 Januari 1970)? 😂

Tenang, HP lu gak lagi kesurupan mesin waktu. Faktanya, komputer itu gak pernah ngerti kalender masehi kayak kita. Mereka cuma ngitung satu hal: total detik yang jalan sejak 1 Januari 1970 (Unix Epoch).

Begitu baterai CMOS atau daya memorinya mati total, hitungannya balik ke detik ke-0. Dan di Indonesia (WIB), detik ke-0 itu jatuhnya persis jam 07:00 pagi tanggal 1 Januari 1970!

Plot twist-nya: sistem hitungan 32-bit ini bakal mentok di tahun 2038 (Y2038 Problem). Menurut kalian, bakal bikin heboh kayak rumor kiamat Y2K dulu gak nih? Tulis di komentar! 👇

#faktateknologi #programming #codinglife #unixepoch #sejarahkomputer #belajarcoding #gasngoding #techtok

title: AI కి మన కంటే ఎక్కువ తెలివి వస్తే?Artificial Intelligence | Science & Technology | AI | AGI | ASI
description:
Meeru YouTube open chesthe, meeku nachhe videos ye vastayi. Instagram lo scroll chesthe, mee taste ki tagga reels vastayi. Google Maps traffic chusi shortcut chupistundi. 

Ivanni chestundi AI. Kaani scientists cheppedi enti ante, idhi AI lo first step matrame. Inka rendu levels unnayi. Avi vasthe prapanchame maripotundi.

Level 1: ANI. Artificial Narrow Intelligence. 

Oka pani lo matrame expert. YouTube AI ki mee taste matrame telusu. 

Maps ki daari matrame telusu. 
Okadaani pani inkokati cheyyaledu. Ippudu manam vaade AI antha ee level lone undi.

Level 2: AGI. Artificial General Intelligence. Manishi laaga edaina nerchukoni cheyyagaladu. 

Oke AI, doctor laaga diagnose chestundi, teacher laaga explain chestundi, engineer laaga design chestundi. 

Edaina Kotha pani ichhina, manishi laaga nerchukuntundi. Ilaanti AI inka raaledu. AI companies konni years lo ee AGI vastundi antunnayi. 

Chala mandi scientists inka chala time padutundi antunnaru. Nijam ga eppudu vastundo evariki teliyadu.

Level 3: ASI ante Artificial Super Intelligence. Ee ASI ki Prapancham lo unna telivaina manushulandari kanna ekkuva telivi untundi. 

Cancer ki mandu, climate change ki solution, years pattey research ni rojullo cheyyochu ee Artificial Super Intelligence.

Kaani ikkade asalu question undi. Manakanna telivaina machine ni manam control cheyyagalama? 

Anduke prapancham antha ippude AI safety, AI rules gurinchi matladutondi.

Mari ee race lo India ekkada undi? Mana government IndiaAI Mission ane pedda plan start chesindi. 

Daani kosam 10,372 crore rupees kharchu chestondi. AI ki GPUs ane powerful computer chips kaavali. Avi AI ki engine lantivi. 

Ippativaraku 38,000 kanna ekkuva GPUs ni ee mission kinda andubatu lo pettaru. 

Vaatitho Sarvam, BharatGen lanti Indian companies and institutes Mana bhashalalo, mana data tho, mana sontha AI models tayaru chestunnaru.

So gurthupettukondi: ippudu manam unnadi Level 1 lo. Level 2, Level 3 ki race already start ayyindi. Aa race lo India kooda undi.

#appsc #appsccurrentaffairs #scienceandtechnology

title: Why Artificial Intelligence Makes Human Skills More Valuable Than Ever
description:
Artificial intelligence is changing the way we work. But does that mean human skills are becoming less important?

Quite the opposite!

In this video, Algo Echo explores seven human skills that may become even more valuable as AI transforms our workplaces.

Discover why these qualities matter:

1. Empathy – understanding and caring for others.
2. Creativity – imagining new possibilities.
3. Critical Thinking – knowing what to question and trust.
4. Communication – bringing people together.
5. Adaptability – remaining willing to learn.
6. Good Judgment – making responsible decisions.
7. Leadership and Collaboration – helping others succeed.

AI can process information and automate many tasks, but human compassion, wisdom, imagination, and understanding remain essential.

The future isn't simply about competing with artificial intelligence. It's about learning how to use technology to bring out our greatest human potential.

At Algo Echo, we believe technology is most valuable when it helps people thrive.

If you enjoyed this video, please like and subscribe to Algo Echo for more friendly, practical insights into artificial intelligence.

Which human skill do you believe will matter most in the future? Share your thoughts in the comments!

title: What Happens When Artificial Intelligence Is Forced to Keep Secrets? 🚀
description:
In this video clip, the speaker discusses the behavior of HAL regarding the power doors, explaining that the AI was instructed to take the astronauts to the monolith while simultaneously being ordered to keep its true nature a secret from them.
Because of this impossible contradiction, the AI concluded that it had to hide the truth, which ultimately led to disaster. The core takeaway is a vital warning for modern technology: never make an AI lie.

title: Investimentos em inteligência artificial ainda não têm retorno mensurável
description:
O retorno dos investimentos em inteligência artificial (IA) ainda não é mensurável para 52% das empresas, segundo a pesquisa Panorama 2027, realizada pela Amcham Brasil em parceria com a Humanizadas, com a participação de 662 executivos. O levantamento mostra interesse das empresas pela tecnologia, mas também aponta dificuldades relacionadas à capacitação e à integração da IA aos negócios.

title: Discover the MSc Big Data & Artificial Intelligence for Business at MBS
description:
Founded in 1897, MBS School of Business is one of France’s longest-established business schools, holding the prestigious AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS triple accreditation. 

Choose a 1- or 2-year programme and earn a state-recognised qualification equivalent to a Master’s-level qualification: the DESSMO (Diplôme d’Études Supérieures Spécialisées en Management des Organisations), recognised at Level 7 in France’s National Register of Professional Qualifications (RNCP). 
Ranked among the Financial Times’ Top 60 Masters in Management, MBS combines academic excellence with an international outlook. Study in Montpellier, a vibrant student city in the south of France, and prepare to shape the future of global supply chains. 

Discover all our MSc programmes: https://www.mbs-education.com/international/our-programmes/programmes-master-of-science/

title: Agentic Finance - Künstliche Intelligenz in der Finanzbranche
description:
Mit Agentic Finance beginnt eine weitere Entwicklungsstufe: KI-Agenten, die eigenständig Informationen analysieren, Zusammenhänge erkennen und daraus Handlungsempfehlungen ableiten.
Was bedeutet das für die Finanzwelt und die Kapitalmärkte? Welche Chancen und Risiken entstehen durch diese Technologie? Und wie müssen sich börsennotierte Unternehmen darauf einstellen, wenn künftig nicht mehr nur Menschen, sondern auch KI-Agenten Geschäftsberichte lesen und Investment Cases bewerten?
Wir sprechen mit Michael Diegelmann, Geschäftsführer der CPT GmbH über die Möglichkeiten von Agentic Finance, die Auswirkungen auf Unternehmen und Investoren und darüber, wie Warren Wise mit seinem Ansatz einen konkreten Mehrwert schaffen möchte.

AI systems are trained using enormous amounts of data to learn patterns, relationships, and connections.

When you ask ChatGPT a question, it processes your input and uses the context and patterns learned during training to generate a response, predicting suitable next tokens one after another.

This is one of the fascinating ideas behind modern AI language models.

But here's the catch: AI doesn't always produce correct answers. It can generate convincing responses that are completely wrong!

Discover how Artificial Intelligence works and understand the technology behind the AI tools we use every day.

title: How Does AI Learn? 🤖 From Mistakes to Intelligence!#Artificial intelligence #Technology #AIEducation
description:
🤖 How Does Artificial Intelligence Learn? | The Science Behind Machine Learning! 🐱

Have you ever wondered how a computer can recognize a cat just by looking at a picture? It might look simple, but behind this ability is an amazing technology called Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).

Imagine teaching a computer what a cat looks like. First, we show it thousands of pictures of different cats. The computer studies these images and tries to understand patterns such as ears, eyes, fur, shapes, and other features.

But here's the interesting part! At first, the computer might make mistakes. It could look at a cat and predict that it is a dog. Does that mean it has failed? Absolutely not!

Every mistake helps the computer improve. Using a process called Backpropagation, the neural network adjusts its connections and learns from its errors. It makes small improvements, tries again, and gradually becomes more accurate.

First, it might predict 38%, then 61%, then 84%. After thousands of learning attempts, it becomes better at recognizing cats.

Finally, when we show it a completely new cat picture that it has never seen before, it can correctly identify it as a CAT! 🐱

This is the basic idea behind Machine Learning: Try → Make Mistakes → Adjust → Learn → Improve!

Just like humans, machines can improve through practice and experience. This is one of the most fascinating things about Artificial Intelligence.

🚀 What you'll learn in this video:

How Artificial Intelligence learns.

What Machine Learning actually means.

How neural networks work.

Why AI makes mistakes.

How computers improve their predictions.

How AI recognizes images it has never seen before.

💡 Technology is changing the world, and understanding how AI works is the first step toward understanding the future!

title: Types of Artificial Intelligence Explained 🤖 | ANI vs AGI vs ASI | AI: Present & Beyond#aishorts
description:
Types of Artificial Intelligence Explained 🤖 | ANI vs AGI vs ASI | AI: Present & Beyond

क्या आप जानते हैं कि Artificial Intelligence के भी अलग-अलग Types होते हैं? 🤔

आज AI सिर्फ सवालों के जवाब देने तक सीमित नहीं है। इसकी दुनिया में Narrow AI से लेकर Artificial Superintelligence तक की कल्पना की जाती है!

इस वीडियो में जानिए:

🤖 1. Narrow AI (ANI) एक खास काम करने में माहिर AI, जैसे Face Recognition और Voice Assistants।

🧠 **2. General AI (AGI) ऐसा AI जो इंसानों की तरह अलग-अलग काम सीख और समझ सके। यह अभी एक शोध का लक्ष्य है।

🚀 **3. Artificial Superintelligence (ASI)भविष्य की एक काल्पनिक अवधारणा, जिसमें AI की बुद्धिमत्ता इंसानों से भी आगे हो सकती है।

title: Человек vs Искусственный Интеллект | Men & Ai
description:
9🤖 А СМОЖЕТ ЛИ ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ ЗАМЕНИТЬ ЧЕЛОВЕЧЕСКИЙ РАЗУМ?

Сегодня ИИ способен писать программы, решать сложные задачи, создавать тексты и даже обучать людей. Но означает ли это, что традиционное образование теряет свою ценность?

Один считает, что главное — научиться управлять искусственным интеллектом. Другой уверен: без фундаментальных знаний человек не сможет даже правильно поставить задачу машине.

Но где проходит граница между человеческим мышлением и возможностями ИИ?

В этом видео — спор о будущем образования, знаниях, самостоятельном мышлении и роли человека в мире искусственного интеллекта.

🔥 А на чьей стороне вы?
Нужно ли сегодня учиться всему самостоятельно или достаточно уметь правильно пользоваться ИИ?

Пишите своё мнение в комментариях. Возможно, именно ваша точка зрения заставит кого-то задуматься!

title: How Invisible Static Fools Artificial Intelligence
description:
First, invisible static tricks an image AI into seeing a gibbon instead of a panda. Funny, right? Until that exact same blind spot happens inside an AI security scanner. Watch how adding 7,000 harmless bytes changes an AI's confidence score from 81% down to 35%—and why real-world cybersecurity always uses Defense in Depth (multiple layers of protection) instead of trusting a single guard.

#cybersecurity #artificialintelligence #tech #computerscience #machinelearning #infosec #cyberdefense #techeducation

title: Why AI Can't Count the R's in Strawberry #ai #artificialintelligence #techfacts #chatgpt  #shorts
description:
AI can write code, but many models have struggled to count the R's in "strawberry." 🍓🤖

The reason: AI doesn't read letters. It reads chunks called tokens.

Newer models often fix it, but the reason it happens is one of the best ways to understand how AI actually works.

Follow for tech facts that sound fake but are real. 💻

title: How a Massive Sea Disappeared: The Aral Sea Disaster #shorts #climatechange
description:
The Aral Sea was once the fourth-largest lake in the world, but today, it is almost entirely completely gone. In the 1960s, the Soviet Union implemented a massive agricultural policy, diverting the two main rivers that fed the sea to irrigate the desert for cotton farming. This single policy cut off the sea's water supply, causing it to shrink rapidly and creating one of the worst human-made environmental disasters in history.

title: 5 Step Solution to Climate Change! | Udit Gupta
description:
We have known how to tackle climate change for over 30 years. The science is clear, and many of the solutions are already available.

Solar energy is becoming cheaper. We know how to reduce air pollution, protect people from floods, improve water conservation and support farmers facing extreme weather.

So why aren't governments acting faster?

In this video, I explain 5 practical steps to tackle climate change, supported by research from Oxfam, the IPCC and the International Energy Agency.

We also examine the less-discussed side of the climate crisis: the influence of fossil fuel companies, corporate lobbying, short-term political decisions, and the lack of accountability in public spending.

From cheaper solar electricity in India to the unequal impact of Mumbai floods, the evidence shows why climate change is not just an environmental issue. It affects our health, food prices, livelihoods, and everyday lives.

And those who contribute least to the problem are often the most vulnerable to its consequences.

Educate. Organise. Agitate.

Understanding the problem is where change begins.

Share this video with someone who wants to understand climate change beyond the usual headlines.

Research and sources:

Oxfam — Disaster Divide: How Climate Chaos Deepens Inequality and Enriches the Few (2026)

IPCC — Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report  
https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/

International Energy Agency — India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026  
https://www.iea.org/reports/india-renewable-energy-market-report-2026

title: Paris Climate Accords and COP31 are Toothless! #unitednations #cop31 #climatechange
description:
GREAT NEWS! THE PARIS CLIMATE AGREEMENT HAS ALL THE TEETH OF A GUMMY BEAR!

Set your own emissions targets! Promise to make progress! And if you miss those targets? SEE YOU AT THE NEXT CONFERENCE!

In this episode of Just a Derp, we explain what the Paris Climate Agreement is, how it connects to COP31, and what actually happens when countries fail to deliver their promised emissions cuts.

Countries must submit plans, report progress, and pursue measures toward their goals. But achieving those national targets? The agreement doesn’t make that legally mandatory, and its compliance committee cannot impose punishments.

No treaty-imposed fines or sanctions for missing your emissions target. Apparently, the planet’s accountability department runs on diplomatic pressure and strongly worded disappointment!

International cooperation and tracking emissions have value. But calling an agreement “legally binding” doesn’t guarantee results.

💬 Can an international climate agreement be effective without real penalties for missing its targets? Tell me in the comments!

But hey, what do I know? I’m Just a Derp!

Political satire and commentary.

title: When climate science enters the courtroom #ClimateChange #ClimateScience #LSE
description:
Can a farmer in the Peruvian Andes hold a German energy company responsible for the glacier melting above his home? In 2015 Saúl Luciano Lliuya sued RWE, Germany's largest electricity producer, for 0.47 per cent of the cost of protecting his town from a swollen glacial lake.

Drawing on his book, "The Climate Trial", Dr Noah Walker-Crawford follows the case from Peru to a courtroom in Germany. He asks what it means to treat climate change as a matter between neighbours, and what happens when climate science is asked to meet a court's standards of proof.

📖 "The Climate Trial: Law and Justice on a Melting Planet" is published by Duke University Press, https://www.dukeupress.edu/the-climat...

🔴 Dr Noah Walker-Crawford is a social anthropologist and Research Fellow at the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment. His research examines how climate science becomes legal evidence. https://www.lse.ac.uk/people/noah-wal... 

🔴 Find out more about the LSE Research Showcase events: https://www.lse.ac.uk/researchshowcase

🔴 Read more about Noah's research in Research for the World, our online social science magazine: https://www.lse.ac.uk/research/resear...

title: Week 1 - What happened at COP31?
description:
Week 1 at COP31 is over. What's next in week 2? Find out!

COP31 is the 31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026.

Twitter ► https://twitter.com/UNFCCC
Instagram ► https://www.instagram.com/UNclimatechange/
TikTok ► https://www.tiktok.com/@unclimatechange
Facebook ► https://www.facebook.com/UNclimatechange 

The UNFCCC secretariat (UN Climate Change) is the United Nations entity tasked with supporting the global response to the threat of climate change. UNFCCC stands for United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The Convention has near universal membership (197 Parties) and is the parent treaty of the 2015 Paris Agreement. The main aim of the Paris Agreement is to keep the global average temperature rise this century as close as possible to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. The UNFCCC is also the parent treaty of the 1997 Kyoto Protocol. The ultimate objective of all three agreements under the UNFCCC is to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that will prevent dangerous human interference with the climate system, in a time frame which allows ecosystems to adapt naturally and enables sustainable development.


 # # #UNClimateChange

title: Can Technology Fight Climate Change? | #3TB
description:
Can technology help us fight climate change and hold polluters accountable?

From construction-site AQI monitoring boards in Mumbai to Climate TRACE's global emissions tracking, technology is opening new ways to monitor pollution and identify emission sources.

In this reel from 3 Techies Banter, the conversation explores how data, sensors and monitoring technologies can help track environmental offenders and make industries more accountable.

Technology may not solve every environmental challenge, but could it be one of our strongest tools in the fight against climate change?

Watch the conversation!

title: COP31 Explained: AI क्यों बना जरूरी? 🧐 !! #physicswallah #cop31 #climatechange #upsc #shorts
description:
COP31 Explained: AI क्यों बना जरूरी? 🧐 !! #physicswallah #cop31 #climatechange #upsc #shorts


Short by Naveen sir: 
68a56bba5f71023eeae2d0742

_____

🌍 COP31 Explained: AI का नया Climate Mission!

क्या Artificial Intelligence (AI) अब Climate Change की सही जानकारी दुनिया तक पहुंचाएगा? COP31 में एक नई पहल का लक्ष्य AI की मदद से Climate Information को अधिक Reliable, Accurate और Accessible बनाना है।

आज के दौर में Climate Misinformation एक बड़ी चुनौती है। ऐसे में AI कैसे Climate Data को समझने और सही जानकारी फैलाने में मदद कर सकता है? जानिए इस नए Global Initiative की पूरी कहानी।

🎯 UPSC Aspirants के लिए क्यों जरूरी?

- COP31 और Climate Change
- Artificial Intelligence (AI)
- Climate Misinformation
- Global Climate Governance
- Environment & International Relations

title: ಮೊಬೈಲ್ ಬಳಕೆ ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಆರೋಗ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಅಪಾಯವೇ? ಹವಾಮಾನ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯೂ ಆತಂಕ! #DigitalHealth #ClimateChange
description:
ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆದ 15ನೇ ಜಾಗತಿಕ ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಉತ್ತೇಜನ ವೇದಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ, ಯುವಜನರ ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಹವಾಮಾನ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯಿಂದ ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತಿರುವ ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ತಜ್ಞರು ಗಂಭೀರ ಚರ್ಚೆ ನಡೆಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ಪರಿಸರದ ಕುರಿತು ಮಂಡಿಸಲಾದ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದಲ್ಲಿ 90 ಲಕ್ಷಕ್ಕೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಯುವಜನರನ್ನು ಒಳಗೊಂಡ 121 ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತ ವಿಮರ್ಶೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. 10ರಿಂದ 24 ವರ್ಷದವರಲ್ಲಿ ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನದ ದುಷ್ಪರಿಣಾಮಗಳು ಪ್ರಯೋಜನಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿರುವುದಾಗಿ ಅಧ್ಯಯನಗಳು ಸೂಚಿಸಿವೆ. ಸುಮಾರು ಶೇ.80ರಷ್ಟು ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿಕೂಲ ಪರಿಣಾಮಗಳನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸಿವೆ.

ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ವೇದಿಕೆಗಳ ಪ್ರಭಾವ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಲು ಆ್ಯಪ್‌ಗಳ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ, ಅಲ್ಗಾರಿದಮ್‌ಗಳ ಪರಿಣಾಮ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪ್ರಾಪ್ತರಿಗೆ ಜಾಹೀರಾತುಗಳ ಮೇಲಿನ ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಗಳನ್ನು ತಜ್ಞರು ಒತ್ತಾಯಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

ಇದೇ ವೇದಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹವಾಮಾನ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ವಾಯುಮಾಲಿನ್ಯದ ಆರೋಗ್ಯದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಪರಿಣಾಮಗಳೂ ಚರ್ಚೆಯಾಗಿವೆ. ವಾಯುಮಾಲಿನ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದಂತೆ ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಮಾರು 70 ಲಕ್ಷ ಸಾವುಗಳು ಸಂಭವಿಸುತ್ತಿವೆ ಎಂದು ಚರ್ಚೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಜಾಗತಿಕ ಇಂಗಾಲದ ಡೈಆಕ್ಸೈಡ್ ಹೊರಸೂಸುವಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾರಿಗೆ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದ ಪಾಲು ಸುಮಾರು ಶೇ.24ರಷ್ಟಿದೆ.

title: ഭൂമി ചൂടുപിടിക്കുകയാണോ? | Climate Change & Eco-Anxiety
description:
​കാലം തെറ്റി പെയ്യുന്ന മഴയും കൊടുംചൂടും നമ്മുടെ പ്ലാനറ്റിനെ മാത്രമല്ല, നമ്മുടെ മാനസികാരോഗ്യത്തെയും ബാധിക്കുന്നുണ്ടോ? കാലാവസ്ഥ വ്യതിയാനവും അത് ഇന്നത്തെ തലമുറയിൽ ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്ന 'Eco-Anxiety' എന്ന അവസ്ഥയെക്കുറിച്ചും ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ സംസാരിക്കുന്നു.

​മാറ്റം നമ്മളിൽ നിന്നുതന്നെ തുടങ്ങാം! ഈ വീഡിയോ ഇഷ്ടപ്പെട്ടാൽ ലൈക്ക് ചെയ്യുക, കൂട്ടുകാരുമായി ഷെയർ ചെയ്യുക. നിങ്ങളുടെ അഭിപ്രായങ്ങൾ താഴെ കമന്റ് ചെയ്യൂ.

title: Why Nobody Stops Polluting (The $0 Problem) #economics #climatechange #shorts
description:
Burning coal costs money, but dumping its smoke into the sky costs nothing. Economists call this an externality. Nobel winner William Nordhaus proposed the fix, a price on carbon, and calculated the "social cost of carbon". The bigger lesson: whatever is free gets wasted.

title: Climate Change Is Shifting Spring—and Bear Food Timing #shorts
description: Since 1950, British Columbia's spring thaw has accelerated by ten days. For bears, this shift creates a dangerous gap between waking up and finding food. A subtle environmental imbalance with long-term consequences for local wildlife. #ClimateChange #BearConservation #WildlifeEcology #EnvironmentalImpact #NatureAlert

title: We Took Climate Change into the Classroom | CELI at JSS Kpaduma, Abuja #Shorts
description:
CELI took the climate conversation into the classroom at Junior Secondary School Kpaduma, Abuja. We talked with students about why hotter days, floods and poor harvests hit families first, and every voice in the room counted.

This visit is part of our work related to the Greening Education Partnership. Young people will live longest with climate change. They deserve a say in the solutions.

Thank you, JSS Kpaduma, for welcoming us.

Climate Energy and Livelihoods Initiative (CELI). Subscribe for more on climate, energy and livelihoods in Nigeria.

title: Climate Change Live: क्या 2050 तक दुनिया खत्म हो जाएगी ? Breaking News | Weather | India News
description:
जलवायु परिवर्तन का संकट अब केवल भविष्य की चेतावनी नहीं, बल्कि पूरी दुनिया के सामने खड़ी एक गंभीर चुनौती बनता जा रहा है। बढ़ता वैश्विक तापमान, पिघलते ग्लेशियर, समुद्र का बढ़ता जलस्तर, बाढ़, सूखा और जंगलों में लगती भीषण आग लोगों के जीवन और उनके घरों को प्रभावित कर रही है। अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रवासन संगठन (IOM) की महानिदेशक एमी पोप ने चेतावनी दी है कि जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रभावों के कारण 2050 तक दुनिया में करीब 21.6 करोड़ लोग अपने घर छोड़ने के लिए मजबूर हो सकते हैं। आखिर क्या दुनिया एक बड़े जलवायु विस्थापन संकट की ओर बढ़ रही है? मुंबई, न्यूयॉर्क, मियामी और मालदीव जैसे तटीय इलाकों के सामने कितनी बड़ी चुनौती है? देखिए जलवायु परिवर्तन के खतरे और मानवता के भविष्य पर यह खास रिपोर्ट।

How is Sindh changing its approach to climate action, and what role can nature play in protecting Pakistan's future? Watch our report to find out.

title: Climate Change: 1880 से 2025 तक धरती के तापमान में आए बड़े बदलाव की वजह क्या है? | NASA | Weather
description:
धरती लगातार गर्म हो रही है और ग्लोबल वार्मिंग की रफ्तार बढ़ रही है. इसकी सबसे बड़ी वजह वातावरण में कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड, मीथेन और नाइट्रस ऑक्साइड जैसी गैसों का लगातार बढ़ना है. title: Climate Change, Explained.
description:
Climate change, explained by an accountant: why 30 years of climate promises haven't cut emissions, and why carbon accounting is what changes that.
Website: https://www.climateaccountants.com.au

We've known since 1856 that CO2 traps heat. We've had 30 years of global climate promises. So why are emissions still going up? The answer is surprisingly simple: you can't cut what you can't count.

In this video I walk through 170 years of climate history in 8 minutes, from Eunice Foote's jar experiment to Rio, Kyoto and Paris. I cover why the promises failed, how the "carbon rulebook" (Scope 1, 2 and 3) works using a café as the example, and why counting carbon like cash is the biggest shift happening right now. I also explain why small businesses are about to start getting emails asking for their emissions data.

NEED HELP WITH CLIMATE REPORTING?
Climate Accountants helps Australian organisations get climate reporting right under AASB S2, the climate standard in the Australian Sustainability Reporting Standards (ASRS). We bring an accountant's approach to carbon: clear numbers, solid evidence and disclosures ready for assurance.

AASB S2 climate reporting: https://climateaccountants.com.au/aasb-s2-climate-reporting/
Carbon accounting: https://climateaccountants.com.au/carbon-accounting/
GHG inventory (Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions): https://climateaccountants.com.au/ghg-inventory-scope-1-2-3/
GHG emissions calculations: https://climateaccountants.com.au/ghg-emissions-calculations/
Climate scenario analysis: https://climateaccountants.com.au/climate-scenario-analysis/
Assurance readiness: https://climateaccountants.com.au/assurance-readiness/
For sustainability advisers: https://climateaccountants.com.au/for-sustainability-advisers/

Whether you're a Group 1, 2 or 3 reporter under Australia's mandatory climate reporting, or a supplier who's just been asked for your emissions data, let's talk: https://climateaccountants.com.au/contact/

CHAPTERS
0:00 The most important climate tool
0:18 The jar experiment
0:38 Eunice Foote, 1856
1:04 We've known for a long time
1:51 The promises: Rio, Kyoto, Paris
2:30 What went wrong
2:49 Where emissions actually come from
3:24 Why businesses?
4:09 The rulebook: Scope 1, 2 and 3
4:26 Scopes explained with a café
5:07 Why nothing changed
5:19 Carbon, treated like cash
6:10 It's spreading fast
6:29 The email coming to your inbox
6:45 The honest bit
7:14 COP31, right now
7:22 Why I'm still optimistic
7:37 What a 1494 accounting book taught us
8:04 See you in the next one

ABOUT
I'm Vishal, Director at Climate Accountants, based in Sydney. We help organisations measure, report and make sense of their carbon, the same way accountants do for money.
https://www.climateaccountants.com.au

CREDITS
Riocentro, Rio-92 venue: Agência CNT de Notícias, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
Kyoto International Conference Center: Marie-Sophie Mejan, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
COP21 site, Le Bourget: A. Bouissou / MEDDE, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
Eunice Foote, "Circumstances Affecting the Heat of the Sun's Rays" (1856): public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
Portrait of Luca Pacioli (1495), attributed to Jacopo de' Barbari: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
Emissions by sector: WRI / Climate Watch (2023 data)
Music: "Deep Urban" by Eugenio Mininni (Mixkit)

This video is general information only, not financial, legal or tax advice.

title: Langzeitstudie zu alpinen Klima-Veränderungen | Südtirol heute vom 10.11.2026
description:
GLORIA: So heißt ein internationales Forschungsprojekt, das seit 25 Jahren hochalpine Landschaften und deren Veränderungen untersucht. Auch Südtirol ist Teil dieser Langzeitstudie. Diese Woche präsentiert das Forschungsteam zum ersten Mal öffentlich die bisherigen Forschungsergebnisse. Wir haben Andreas Hilpold, den Leiter des Südtirol-Teams vorab getroffen.

ORF Südtirol liefert für dich auch auf YouTube aktuelle Berichte, emotionale Reportagen und spannende Interviews. Wir fragen nach, was die Menschen in Südtirol bewegt und sind dabei, wenn im Land etwas passiert.

Abonniere unseren ORF Südtirol-Kanal, um keine Videos zu verpassen.

title: Clearcut Logging creates more Floods than Climate Change does - New study from UBC
description:
In recent years, flooding has become one of the largest and most damaging disruptions across North America.

These events are often blamed on climate change, and while changes such as warming weather and increasing rainfall can contribute to flooding, climate change isn’t the biggest factor here. Human activity can often play an even greater role in determining how frequent and severe floods are.

Logging has long been shown to be one of the most significant contributing factors to more extreme floods, yet with profitability and wood volume of harvests being top priorities for forest management, the impacts of clearcut logging are still largely unconsidered at the landscape level.  It’s only been until very recently that we’ve been able to quantify exactly how much logging amplifies these impacts, with a new study from Younes Alila's lab at @ubcforestry finding that the largest, rarest and most destructive floods were the most sensitive to logging disturbance.

This study looked at a watershed in interior BC where, as a result of anthropogenic climate change, the snowfall has been gradually decreasing, which would therefore reduce flood risk and lead to flood events happening less frequently. However, clearcut logging of about 40% of the watershed was enough to more than offset the climate-driven reduction in flood risk. When the effect of harvesting was isolated, flood frequency increased dramatically: what would have been a 50-year flood without logging occurred every 3 years after clearcut logging.  So while a changing climate has reduced flood risk in this watershed, the isolated effect of logging made these large floods about 16 times more frequent - that’s insane.

In the case of increased flooding, climate change is often just a scapegoat to the real problem here - ongoing clearcut logging.  If we want to create safe, healthy lands and waters with reduced risk to our communities, then it’s time we listen to what the science says and stop clearcut logging, to instead implement more ecologically sound harvest practices that work to create better futures for all of us.

#flood #ubc #logging #hydrology #forestry #forest #climate #crisis #clearcut #river #BC

clean_text: Clearcut Logging creates more Floods than Climate Change does - New study from UBC In recent years, flooding has become one of the largest and most damaging disruptions across North America. These events are often blamed on climate change, and while changes such as warming weather and increasing rainfall can contribute to flooding, climate change isn’t the biggest factor here. Human activity can often play an even greater role in determining how frequent and severe floods are. Logging has long been shown to be one of the most significant contributing factors to more extreme floods, yet with profitability and wood volume of harvests being top priorities for forest management, the impacts of clearcut logging are still largely unconsidered at the landscape level. It’s only been until very recently that we’ve been able to quantify exactly how much logging amplifies these impacts, with a new study from Younes Alila's lab at @ubcforestry finding that the largest, rarest and most destructive floods were the most sensitive to logging disturbance. This study looked at a watershed in interior BC where, as a result of anthropogenic climate change, the snowfall has been gradually decreasing, which would therefore reduce flood risk and lead to flood events happening less frequently. However, clearcut logging of about 40% of the watershed was enough to more than offset the climate-driven reduction in flood risk. When the effect of harvesting was isolated, flood frequency increased dramatically: what would have been a 50-year flood without logging occurred every 3 years after clearcut logging. So while a changing climate has reduced flood risk in this watershed, the isolated effect of logging made these large floods about 16 times more frequent - that’s insane. In the case of increased flooding, climate change is often just a scapegoat to the real problem here - ongoing clearcut logging. If we want to create safe, healthy lands and waters with reduced risk to our communities, then it’s time we listen to what the science says and stop clearcut logging, to instead implement more ecologically sound harvest practices that work to create better futures for all of us. #flood #ubc #logging #hydrology #forestry #forest #climate #crisis #clearcut #river #BC

title: Did climate change kill the Aral Sea?
description:
Drier years made things worse, but the main cause of the Aral's collapse was river water diverted for irrigation. Climate change may add pressure in the future: the IPCC expects the Amu Darya basin could face severe water scarcity by mid-century. Full story: How to Make a Sea Disappear.

Sources: Micklin (2007); IPCC AR6 WGII, Ch. 10 (2022).

title: Climate change, shifting fisheries and lack of infrastructure shrink Greenland’s coastal settlements
description:
(10 Nov 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilulissat, Greenland - 30 October 2026

1. Sun rising as boat departs Ilulissat port 
2. Various of boat sailing to small settlement of Oqaatsut
3. Various of skipper sailing boat 
4. Pan of iceberg as boat sails by

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Oqaatsut, Greenland - 30 October 2026

5. Various of Oqaatsut homes as boat arrives
6. Pan of Oqaatsut, homes and ice in harbor
7. Boats moored in harbor
8. Ice in harbor
9. Various of Aron. S. Skade, 19-year-old fisherman and Oqaatsut resident, preparing fishing lines on boat 
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Aron. S. Skade, 19-year-old fisherman and Oqaatsut resident:
"It's calm sometimes and snow is really fun. Everything about it is just really calm, but sometimes the wind is just too much and it sucks."

11. Various of Oqaatsut, homes and ice in harbor
12. Muskox and reindeer heads on shed 
13. Various of sled dogs
14. SOUNDBITE (English) Aron. S. Skade, 19-year-old fisherman and Oqaatsut resident:
"It's my first time having dogs, and I don't want anything more than just... I just want dogs. Going to the mountains, the view is very beautiful. And just going on a boat and ride, sometimes hunting. It's very calming and just get things off your mind."

15. Various of fisherman preparing lines 
16. Wide of fisherman and boat

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Copenhagen, Denmark - 9 November 2026

17. Setup shot of Kåre Hendriksen, associate professor, Arctic Civil Engineering, Technical University of Denmark (DTU), speaking during interview
18. SOUNDBITE (English) Kåre Hendriksen, associate professor, Arctic Civil Engineering, Technical University of Denmark (DTU):
"If you go back to the end of the Second World War, there was living 20,000 people in Greenland. And the majority (were) living in the small settlements. So, everybody in Greenland has relation back to a small settlement. And the culture in Greenland is based on the stories about hunting. People (were) living by hunting. And if you're living off hunting, you need to live few people on a location."

19. Cutaway of Hendriksen speaking 
20. SOUNDBITE (English) Kåre Hendriksen, associate professor, Arctic Civil Engineering, Technical University of Denmark (DTU):
"We will lose some settlements in the coming years. There's no doubt about that. But it's a political decision whether you want to keep the remaining settlements or not."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilulissat, Greenland - 31 October 2026

21. Aerial shot of iceberg in Ilulissat Icefjord ++MUTE++
22. Aerial shot of fishing boat sailing by huge iceberg ++MUTE++
23. Aerial shot of Ilulissat coastline and homes ++MUTE++
24. Various of snow-covered buildings by coastline

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilulissat, Greenland - 2 November 2026

25. Local municipality office building exterior
26. Greenlandic flag flying 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilulissat, Greenland - 3 November 2026

27. Various setup shots of Lars Erik Gabrielsen, Mayor of Avannaata Municipality and member of Siumut political party, working at desk
28. Cutaway of painting, showing Oqaatsut
29. SOUNDBITE (English) Lars Erik Gabrielsen, Mayor of Avannaata Municipality and member of Siumut political party:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilulissat, Greenland - 31 October 2026

30. Fishing boat sailing by iceberg in Ilulissat Icefjord
31. Icebergs in tide by coastline 
32. Icebergs seen behind rocks 
33. Icebergs in Ilulissat Icefjord

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ilulissat, Greenland - 1 November 2026

34. Various of apartment blocks, known as "Little Qullissat”, established to house families relocated from Qullissat when it was closed 

ASSOCIATED PRESS

description:
जलवायु परिवर्तन का संकट अब केवल भविष्य की चेतावनी नहीं, बल्कि पूरी दुनिया के सामने खड़ी एक गंभीर चुनौती बनता जा रहा है। बढ़ता वैश्विक तापमान, पिघलते ग्लेशियर, समुद्र का बढ़ता जलस्तर, बाढ़, सूखा और जंगलों में लगती भीषण आग लोगों के जीवन और उनके घरों को प्रभावित कर रही है। अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रवासन संगठन (IOM) की महानिदेशक एमी पोप ने चेतावनी दी है कि जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रभावों के कारण 2050 तक दुनिया में करीब 21.6 करोड़ लोग अपने घर छोड़ने के लिए मजबूर हो सकते हैं। आखिर क्या दुनिया एक बड़े जलवायु विस्थापन संकट की ओर बढ़ रही है? मुंबई, न्यूयॉर्क, मियामी और मालदीव जैसे तटीय इलाकों के सामने कितनी बड़ी चुनौती है? देखिए जलवायु परिवर्तन के खतरे और मानवता के भविष्य पर यह खास रिपोर्ट।
The climate change crisis is no longer just a warning for the future; it has become a grave challenge facing the entire world. Rising global temperatures, melting glaciers, sea-level rise, floods, droughts, and intense forest fires are taking a toll on people’s lives and their homes. Amy Pope, Director General of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), has warned that by 2050, the impacts of climate change could force approximately 216 million people worldwide to leave their homes. Is the world heading toward a major climate-induced displacement crisis? How significant is the challenge facing coastal regions such as Mumbai, New York, Miami, and the Maldives? Explore this special report on the threat of climate change and the future of humanity.

title: Climate Change Live: 2050 तक बदल जाएगी दुनिया की तस्वीर | Breaking News | Weather | India News
description:
जलवायु परिवर्तन का संकट अब केवल भविष्य की चेतावनी नहीं, बल्कि पूरी दुनिया के सामने खड़ी एक गंभीर चुनौती बनता जा रहा है। बढ़ता वैश्विक तापमान, पिघलते ग्लेशियर, समुद्र का बढ़ता जलस्तर, बाढ़, सूखा और जंगलों में लगती भीषण आग लोगों के जीवन और उनके घरों को प्रभावित कर रही है। अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रवासन संगठन (IOM) की महानिदेशक एमी पोप ने चेतावनी दी है कि जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रभावों के कारण 2050 तक दुनिया में करीब 21.6 करोड़ लोग अपने घर छोड़ने के लिए मजबूर हो सकते हैं। आखिर क्या दुनिया एक बड़े जलवायु विस्थापन संकट की ओर बढ़ रही है? मुंबई, न्यूयॉर्क, मियामी और मालदीव जैसे तटीय इलाकों के सामने कितनी बड़ी चुनौती है? देखिए जलवायु परिवर्तन के खतरे और मानवता के भविष्य पर यह खास रिपोर्ट।

title: Marcos: Geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty, climate change reshaping Southeast Asia fast
description:
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., in his opening remarks for the 49th ASEAN Summit on Sunday morning said that 11 ASEAN members that differ in size, history and culture have come together on a shared journey for the region. "We come as equals, carrying the hopes of our peoples and a shared responsibility to transform them into a common purpose," he said as he referenced the pre-hispanic balangay boat in the summit logo. He said the region faces "shifting tides" that include geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty, new technologies, climate change, and transnational threats. He said the delegates have chosen to come to Manila  to "travel forward together."

title: Klimawandel in hochalpinen Gebieten
description:
Wie verändert der Klimawandel unsere Bergwelt? Seit 25 Jahren untersucht das internationale Forschungsprojekt GLORIA die Entwicklung hochalpiner Ökosysteme. Weltweit werden dafür dieselben Messungen in regelmäßigen Abständen wiederholt. Die Langzeitmessungen zeigen, dass wärmeliebende Pflanzen immer weiter nach oben vordringen, während spezialisierte Arten der höchsten Gipfellagen zunehmend unter Druck geraten. Ein Wandel, der die empfindlichen Lebensräume nachhaltig verändert.

#orf #stheute #klimawandel #hochalpin #lebensraum

title: China Flew Electric Plane ✈️| #china #ElectriAirplane #shorts #viralvideo #india #technology
description:
China Flew Electric Plane ✈️| #china #ElectriAirplane #shorts #viralvideo #india #technology  

China flew a 10-ton electric plane with zero fuel. The COMAC CE-25A electric aircraft completed its first crewed test flight on 14 November 2026 in Shandong, running only on batteries. Two pilots and one flight test engineer were on board. The CE-25A is a 19-seat electric commercial aircraft developed by COMAC with battery maker CATL, with a target range of 400 to 500 km for short domestic routes.

There is no date yet for passenger service, so this is the start of electric aviation, not the finish. In this video we explain why China is moving from electric cars to electric planes, what it means for oil dependency and renewable energy, and why India should start building in this space. When do you think India will have its own electric plane? Share your view in the comments.

description:

Live Demo: Geeta Agro Industries' New Advanced Peanut Harvester Thresher! 🚜🥜

નમસ્કાર ખેડૂત મિત્રો! 🚜🙏

આજના ખાસ વીડિયોમાં અમે તમારા માટે લાવ્યા છીએ ગીતા એગ્રો ઈન્ડસ્ટ્રીઝ (Jasdan) દ્વારા બનાવવામાં આવેલ અદ્યતન 'મગફળી કાઢવાના હાર્વેસ્ટર' (Peanut Harvester/Thresher) નો લાઈવ ડેમો!

આ હાર્વેસ્ટર મગફળીના પાકને જમીનમાંથી ખોદીને, સાફ કરીને સીધો ટ્રેક્ટરમાં ભરવા માટે સક્ષમ છે. 

આ આધુનિક ટેક્નોલોજીથી ખેડૂતોનો સમય અને મજૂરી ખર્ચ બંનેમાં મોટી બચત થશે.

વીડિયોની મુખ્ય વિશેષતાઓ:
✅ મગફળી ખોદવાની નવી પદ્ધતિ.
✅ ખેતરમાં લાઈવ કામગીરીનો ડેમો.
✅ સમય અને પૈસાની બચત કરતા મશીનની માહિતી.

જો તમને આ મશીન ગમ્યું હોય અથવા ખરીદવાની ઈચ્છા હોય, તો ગીતા એગ્રો ઈન્ડસ્ટ્રીઝ, જસદણનો સંપર્ક કરી શકો છો (તમારો સંપર્ક નંબર અહીં ઉમેરો).

description:
WAIT… TUMHARA ELECTRIC IRON KHUD KAISE JAANTA HAI KAB BAND HONA HAI? ⚡🤯

Tum iron ko ON karke kapde press karte ho, aur kuch der baad uska heater automatically OFF ho jaata hai. Phir thanda hone par dobara ON!

Lekin ye magic nahi, science hai! 🔬

title: 🚂 The Evolution of Train Braking Technology #cafevibes #dessert #easyrecipes #edm #engineering
description:
Witness the incredible mechanical journey of locomotive deceleration throughout history. From the raw, physical exertion required to operate a nineteenth-century manual hand-brake to the precise, high-speed engineering of modern disc assemblies, this video explores the innovation behind bringing massive trains to a safe stop. 

We begin with the gritty, atmospheric labor of steam-era rail workers before transitioning to the sparks and heavy industrial grit of mid-twentieth-century diesel braking systems. As technology advances, we delve into the high-tech reality of contemporary high-speed express trains, where hydraulic systems and advanced friction materials manage intense heat and speed. Finally, we step into the future of rail travel, analyzing the sophisticated digital interfaces and automated emergency braking systems that define modern Maglev and high-speed bullet train safety. This visual montage provides an immersive look at the engineering milestones that have shaped transport history and ensured passenger safety for generations. Discover how the fundamental mechanics of friction have evolved into the complex electronic networks of tomorrow.

#trains #engineering #technology #locomotive #history

title: Kaynes Technology Crashes 15%: Four Big Concerns Investors Must Watch
description:
Kaynes Technology shares plunged nearly 15% following a disappointing Q2 performance, raising fresh concerns about the company's growth momentum, profitability and cash flows.

Revenue growth remained muted for the second consecutive quarter, while EBITDA margins contracted and net profit declined sharply. Adding to investor concerns are rising receivables and inventory, lower cash balances, and the restatement of FY26 financials.

In this Stock of the Day analysis, we break down four key concerns facing Kaynes Technology:

- **Capital Raise:** Receivables and inventory have swelled to nearly ₹3,000 crore, while cash balances have declined.
- **Restated Financials:** The company has revised its FY26 profits, raising questions around accounting disclosures.
- **Smart Meter Business:** Management is considering moving the metering business into a separate SPV.
- **Cash Flow Outlook:** The expected timeline for cash flow breakeven has been pushed back, adding to investor concerns.

With growth slowing and cash flow pressures persisting, what lies ahead for Kaynes Technology investors?

title: Kaynes Technology Crashes 20% After Q2 Results: Are EMS Stocks Still Worth Buying?
description:
Kaynes Technology shares plunged nearly 20% after disappointing September quarter results, with revenue growth slowing to 4% and margins declining by 320 basis points to 13.2%. The company's auditor also raised concerns over its investment in associate firm Iskraemeco, adding to investor uncertainty. Chakri Lokapriya, Managing Partner, RSB LLP, explains why Kaynes Technology's challenges are company-specific and discusses the outlook for the broader EMS sector, including Dixon Technologies and Amber Enterprises. With tariff-related pressures easing but supply chain disruptions and expensive valuations remaining concerns, should investors wait for better valuations or stronger earnings growth before investing?

text:

Climate change isn't just about rising temperatures. It's also about our economy, politics, public health, food security, and the powerful interests shaping our future.

If you want to understand the science, the solutions, and why governments struggle to act, here are five books worth reading:

📗 1. The Climate Solution — Mridula Ramesh

A great starting point for Indian readers. Explains how climate change affects our water, food, cities, and everyday lives, and what we can do about it.

📘 2. The New Climate War — Michael E. Mann

Explains how fossil fuel interests, misinformation, and corporate lobbying have delayed climate action and shifted responsibility onto ordinary people.

📙 3. India in a Warming World — Edited by Navroz K. Dubash

To understand India's climate policies, development challenges, international negotiations, and the difficult choices facing our country.

📕 4. The Great Derangement — Amitav Ghosh

Why have our politicians, institutions, and even our culture struggled to take climate change seriously?

📒 5. The Climate Book — Greta Thunberg

A collection of explanations by leading scientists and experts covering the science of climate change, its consequences, and possible solutions.

clean_text: Nailed it. Love this. We need to be smarter about logging and we need to think “down stream”. Logging that contributes to massive floods that then cause billions of dollars of damage needs to be banned. Harvesting old growth needs to be banned. Lumber needs to be harvested only where it won’t contribute to this type of destruction and better logging practices other than clear cutting need to be implemented far away from cities and sensitive ecosystems. People need lumber but excess profit and industry growth should not be anywhere near the top priority. Canada can have a profitable lumber industry if the resources are only used for necessity not excessive exports and excessive building within our own country. Yes, we have a housing shortage but urban sprawl needs to slowed, foreign property investment needs to be banned or at the very least extremely altered. Canada doesn’t require 50 different fast food chains going up in new strip malls all over the country for example. We need food security and environmental/ecological security.

clean_text: Great video and interesting premise/critical to discuss with others. I moved from coastal to rural western NH and even that change has been culturally very difficult. Places are different from each other in so many ways. Even just moving from a small city to a place that is rural was a giant lifestyle change. No real delivery food options and just not many food options, in general. Traveling 40 minutes or more to the doctor. Having only one grocery store option. Being somewhat physically (and therefore) more socially isolated. People have always moved to and from places, and I am less concerned about the ability to build infrastructure to exist for people, should they move, because humans are actually amazing at building infrastructure when we plan and work together. It’s really the planning and working together part that scares me, and it’s harder to figure out how to do that in a rural place, I think. Working on it, for sure.

clean_text: Eine vom CO2-Treibhauseffekt verursachte Erwärmung, messbar mit einem Thermometer, lässt sich experimentell auch mit 100% CO2 nicht nachweisen, weil sein Wärmeleitwert die Temperaturentwicklung bestimmt. Wird im Experiment das CO2 mit dem Treibhausgas CH4 ersetzt, fällt dies sofort auf. Wärmeleitwerte haben aber alle Gase. Deshalb bestimmen auch die 78% Stickstoff und 21% Sauerstoff die Temperatur der Atmosphäre. Am Wärmetransport durch Konvektion sind ebenfalls alle Gase beteiligt (das CO2 mit seinen 0,04%), wobei die Konvektion viel effektiver ist. Für den Wärmetransport über die Verdunstung und Kondensation ist nur das Wasser in der Atmosphäre verantwortlich. Wasser hat auch einen viel größeren Treibhauseffekt als das CO2. Die vom CO2-Treibhauseffekt absorbierte und emittierte Strahlung liegt zwischen 13µm und 17µm, hat also eine Bandbreite von 4µm. Strahlung erzeugt Wärme immer mit einem ganzen Spektrum. Das von der Erde emittierte Strahlungsspektrum liegt zwischen 2µm und über 200µm. Selbst wenn für diese Breite 100µm angenommen wird (weil Glockenkurve) und nicht berücksichtigt wird, dass nur 50% der Strahlung vom CO2 zurück in Richtung Erde emittiert wird, sind die 4µm von 100μm nur 4% vom Spektrum. Als Leistung hat das Strahlungsspektrum der Erde etwa 235W/m². Würde die Atmosphäre aus 100% CO2 bestehen, wären 4% von 235W/m² nur 9,4 W/m². Wir haben aber 0,04% CO2 in der Atmosphäre, was 0,094W/m² ergibt. Geht man von einer Luftsäule von 50 Km aus, wären das 50 000m³, die von diesen 0,094W erwärmt werden. Ein 16m² Zimmer hat 40m³ und braucht 2 500W, um warm zu werden. Die Daten sind überprüfbar und mit den vier Begriffen 1.Wärmeleitwerte Gase, 2.Absorptionsspektren Gase, 3. Planksches Strahlungsspektrum, 4.Wärmestrahlung der Erde von Google leicht zu finden.

text:
Eine vom  CO2-Treibhauseffekt verursachte Erwärmung, messbar mit einem Thermometer, lässt sich experimentell auch mit 100% CO2 nicht nachweisen, weil sein Wärmeleitwert die Temperaturentwicklung bestimmt. 
Wird im Experiment das CO2 mit dem Treibhausgas  CH4  ersetzt, fällt dies sofort auf. 
Wärmeleitwerte haben aber alle Gase. Deshalb bestimmen auch die 78% Stickstoff und 21% Sauerstoff die Temperatur der Atmosphäre. 
Am Wärmetransport durch Konvektion sind ebenfalls alle Gase beteiligt (das CO2 mit seinen 0,04%), wobei die Konvektion viel effektiver ist. Für den Wärmetransport über die Verdunstung und Kondensation ist nur das Wasser in der Atmosphäre verantwortlich. Wasser hat auch einen viel größeren Treibhauseffekt als das CO2. 
Die vom CO2-Treibhauseffekt absorbierte und emittierte Strahlung liegt zwischen 13µm und 17µm, hat also eine Bandbreite von 4µm. Strahlung erzeugt Wärme immer mit einem ganzen Spektrum.
Das von der Erde emittierte Strahlungsspektrum liegt zwischen 2µm und über 200µm. Selbst wenn für diese Breite 100µm angenommen wird  (weil Glockenkurve) und nicht berücksichtigt wird, dass nur 50% der Strahlung vom CO2 zurück in Richtung Erde emittiert wird, sind die 4µm von 100μm nur 4% vom Spektrum.
Als Leistung hat das Strahlungsspektrum der Erde etwa 235W/m². Würde die Atmosphäre aus 100% CO2 bestehen, wären 4% von 235W/m² nur 9,4 W/m². Wir haben aber 0,04% CO2 in der Atmosphäre, was 0,094W/m² ergibt. Geht man von einer Luftsäule von 50 Km aus, wären das 50 000m³, die von diesen 0,094W erwärmt werden. Ein 16m² Zimmer hat 40m³ und braucht 2 500W, um warm zu werden.
Die Daten sind überprüfbar und mit den vier Begriffen 1.Wärmeleitwerte Gase,  2.Absorptionsspektren Gase, 3. Planksches Strahlungsspektrum,  4.Wärmestrahlung der Erde von Google leicht zu finden.
